scope: Static exact-source delta review only. No script, test, host, provider, database, browser, or credential operation was performed.
accepted_delta: The platform child identity now comes from systemd User, Group, and SupplementaryGroups; its UID must be present in the retained allowed-UID argument.
Snapshots include API/checker launch identity, MainPID, and InvocationID, so a concurrent rollout between prepare and activate causes a fail-closed snapshot mismatch.
The installer checks the API launch follows site-current/infra/launch.py and checks the restarted API process cwd resolves to the new overlay.
SIGTERM is converted to InterruptedError and enters the existing exception/finally path.

blocking_finding.summary: Recovery flags are armed after the filesystem mutations they are meant to recover from.
locations: In activate(), the drop-in is created by fresh(DROP, ...) before changed=True.
In activate(), site-current is replaced with the candidate symlink before api_changed=True.
blocking_finding.impact: A SIGTERM can be delivered after a mutation succeeds but before the following flag assignment. The exception handler then skips the corresponding cleanup/rollback. For site-current, the exact pointer test inside rollback makes it safe to reconcile unconditionally or to arm the flag before os.replace. For the drop-in, an interruption during creation can also leave an owned partial file; cleanup should track the exclusively created inode or use a staged atomic replacement, rather than relying only on a flag assigned after fresh() returns.
blocking_finding.required_before_run: Make recovery state cover the mutation itself, including interrupted/partial exclusive drop-in creation; preserve exact ownership predicates so unrelated files or pointers are never removed.
